lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Héctor, it's Yolanda. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How have you been feeling since we last talked?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Pretty good actually.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you cook on Sundays?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that finding the time keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It feels like a lot right now.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Cooking a big pot on Sunday can cover two or three dinners.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: After treatment I had no energy at all.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Cooking a big pot on Sunday can cover two or three dinners.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I got home late every day this week. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're giving everything to work right now, and there's not much left over for you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the cooking at home going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I don't really see the point.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe cook at home 3 nights?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, so your plan this week is to cook at home 3 nights. Did I get that right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Héctor, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

flags.reason: Repeats the same Sunday cooking tip after participant's sustain talk at 42 and 44 without asking permission or exploring.
Strong change talk ('I really want to feel like myself again') was not reflected; coach moved to a new question.
Credits participant with figuring something out on his own that he did not actually say.
'I don't really see the point' was met with a plan prompt rather than exploring the doubt.

score.summary: Yolanda set a clear agenda, used several complex reflections, and helped Héctor set a concrete goal of cooking at home three nights. However, she repeated a tip after sustain talk, missed a strong change statement, and did not review the prior goal or plan around his work-hour barrier.
strengths: Line 28: complex reflection captured Héctor's ambivalence and wish for a plan that fits his life.
Line 49: emphasized autonomy with 'It's your plan', supporting his choice.
Line 52: summarized the agreed goal and checked accuracy before closing.
coaching_tips: Line 43: after sustain talk at 42 and 44, ask permission or explore barriers rather than repeating the same suggestion.
Line 46: reflect the change talk ('You really want to feel like yourself again') and ask what that would look like before moving on.
Line 20: only affirm what the participant actually said; here he had not yet described figuring it out himself.
Line 48: explore 'I don't really see the point' with an open question about what makes cooking feel pointless to him.
